question.worked_solution:
First, we use the algebra of limits to pull out the constant factor of $-3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-3}{{x}^{8}} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }[-3\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{8}}] \\  & =-3\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{8}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{1}{{x}^{8}})=0,
$$

we can evaluate our limit as follows:

$$
-3\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{8}}=-3\cdot 0=0
$$
